description: Experience the fresh, simple flavors of the Aegean with this classic Turkish Grilled Sea Bass recipe, known as Levrek. This dish highlights the natural sweetness of the fish, perfectly complemented by a light marinade of olive oil, lemon, and aromatic herbs. It is a healthy and incredibly satisfying meal that brings the taste of a seaside Turkish restaurant right to your home.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sea Bass
instructions.text: Rinse the cleaned sea bass thoroughly under cold water and pat dry inside and out with paper towels. Make 2-3 diagonal slits on both sides of each fish, about 1/2 inch deep, to help the marinade penetrate and ensure even cooking.

instructions.title: Make the Herb Marinade
instructions.text: In a small bowl, combine the olive oil, juice from one lemon, minced garlic, chopped fresh parsley, chopped fresh dill, salt, and black pepper. Mix well to create a fragrant marinade.

instructions.title: Marinate the Fish
instructions.text: Generously rub the herb marinade all over the sea bass, making sure to get inside the cavities and into the slits. Place a few lemon slices and a sprig of fresh dill or parsley into each fish cavity. Let the fish marinate at room temperature for 15-20 minutes, or refrigerate for up to 30 minutes.

instructions.title: Preheat the Grill
instructions.text: Preheat your outdoor grill or a grill pan over medium-high heat. Ensure the grates are clean. Lightly brush the grates with olive oil to prevent the fish from sticking.

instructions.title: Grill the Sea Bass
instructions.text: Place the marinated sea bass on the hot grill. Grill for 7-10 minutes per side, depending on the thickness of the fish, until the skin is crispy and charred in spots, and the flesh is opaque and flakes easily with a fork. Avoid overcooking to keep the fish moist.

instructions.title: Serve Immediately
instructions.text: Carefully transfer the grilled sea bass to a serving platter. Garnish with fresh lemon wedges and a sprinkle of additional fresh parsley or dill. Serve hot with a simple green salad, Turkish Shepherd's Salad (Çoban Salata), or roasted vegetables.

tips: Always choose the freshest possible sea bass for the best flavor; look for clear eyes and firm flesh.
Do not over-marinate delicate fish like sea bass; 20-30 minutes is usually sufficient to infuse flavor without altering texture.
Ensure your grill is properly preheated and oiled to prevent the fish from sticking and to achieve a beautiful crispy skin.
